title: The Team Warm-Up
story:
Before the evening match, the Riverside team met on the small pitch behind the community hall. The captain, Hana, checked that everyone had water. She told the players to leave their bags by the bench and line up. Hana blew her whistle once, and the group started a slow jog around the pitch.

They ran two easy laps and then moved to the centre circle. Hana led stretches for the legs, the back, and the shoulders. She reminded them that cold muscles can pull. Each player held a stretch and counted to twenty. Young Mateo said his left calf felt tight. Hana told Mateo to ease off and not to bounce.

Next they worked on their joints. They circled their ankles, swung their arms, and lifted their knees. The coach, Idris, walked between them and corrected a few positions. Idris said the warm-up should make the body ready, not tired. He kept the knee lifts short and added a simple passing drill. The players called for the ball and moved it quickly along the ground. They still had eight minutes before the match. Hana gathered the team and asked each person to name one aim. Several players said they would talk more on the pitch. Mateo said he would listen to his calf and speak up if it hurt. Hana smiled and put the whistle away. The warm-up was finished, and the players felt focused for the match.

Inside the community hall
At the river swimming pool
On the school running track

To run three extra laps
To leave the pitch immediately
To jump higher than the others

Twenty minutes
Half an hour

A fast sprint to the goal
A long stretch for the shoulders
A team talk before the match

quiz.question: Why did Hana ask every player to name an aim?

She needed to choose a new captain
She was checking who had forgotten water
She planned to cancel the match
